scenes.tts: How can white flowers disappear, then return in the next generation? Crossing a true-breeding purple pea plant with a white one gives only purple offspring. Later, white flowers return among their descendants.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP for both films: dominant alleles purple, recessive alleles white, grids green, probability markers yellow, neutral labels pale blue. Fill the frame with a moving pea-family timeline. A purple parent flower labelled true-breeding and a white parent flower slide together; purple offspring grow, then one white descendant blooms. Keep a large question mark drifting above the white flower.
scenes.narration: How can white flowers disappear, then return in the next generation? Crossing a true-breeding purple pea plant with a white one gives only purple offspring. Later, white flowers return among their descendants.

scenes.visual: The family timeline holds. Title appears briefly above it: Where the White Was Hiding. Leaves continue swaying.

scenes.tts: The flower-color gene comes in different versions, called alleles. We will track a purple allele and a white allele. Each plant carries a pair.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the purple offspring. Two large allele cards emerge from it: P in purple and p in white. Keep the plant below, filling most of the frame. On-screen labels: gene, alleles, pair.
scenes.narration: The flower-color gene comes in different versions, called alleles. We will track a purple allele and a white allele. Each plant carries a pair.

scenes.tts: The original purple parent carried only purple alleles. The white parent carried only white alleles. Their offspring received one allele from each parent.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the two original parents. Show PP cards inside the purple plant and pp cards inside the white plant. One card from each slides into every purple offspring, forming Pp.
scenes.narration: The original purple parent carried only purple alleles. The white parent carried only white alleles. Their offspring received one allele from each parent.

scenes.tts: That allele pair is the genotype. The visible flower color is the phenotype. This plant looks purple, yet it still carries white.
scenes.visual: Place the P and p cards inside a large plant outline labelled genotype: Pp. The purple flower above gains the label phenotype: purple. The white p card pulses behind the purple bloom instead of disappearing.
scenes.narration: That allele pair is the genotype. The visible flower color is the phenotype. This plant looks purple, yet it still carries white.

scenes.tts: Matching allele pairs are homozygous. A mixed pair is heterozygous. The first-generation plants are heterozygous, which explains how the white allele stays present.
scenes.visual: Arrange PP, Pp and pp allele cards across the frame. Brackets group PP and pp under homozygous. Pp moves under heterozygous, then returns inside the purple first-generation plant.
scenes.narration: Matching allele pairs are homozygous. A mixed pair is heterozygous. The first-generation plants are heterozygous, which explains how the white allele stays present.

scenes.tts: Here, the purple allele is dominant, so one copy makes purple flowers. The white allele is recessive, so white appears only when no purple allele is present.
scenes.visual: Transform the plant into three side-by-side genotype panels: PP and Pp bloom purple; pp blooms white. A purple overlay covers the white card only in Pp. On-screen note: complete dominance in this pea model.
scenes.narration: Here, the purple allele is dominant, so one copy makes purple flowers. The white allele is recessive, so white appears only when no purple allele is present.

scenes.tts: Dominant does not mean common, stronger, or more likely to be passed on. It describes which phenotype appears when the two alleles differ.
scenes.visual: Keep the Pp plant centered. Cross out three drifting labels: common, stronger, passed on more. Replace them with one label pointing to the bloom: phenotype with a mixed pair.
scenes.narration: Dominant does not mean common, stronger, or more likely to be passed on. It describes which phenotype appears when the two alleles differ.

scenes.tts: When a plant makes sex cells, its allele pair separates during meiosis. A heterozygous plant therefore makes both kinds in about equal numbers.
scenes.visual: Return to one large Pp plant. Its paired P and p cards pull apart along two paths into a flowing stream of sex cells. Alternating purple P and white p cells drift continuously. On-screen label: segregation.
scenes.narration: When a plant makes sex cells, its allele pair separates during meiosis. A heterozygous plant therefore makes both kinds in about equal numbers.

scenes.tts: Fertilization brings one sex cell from each parent together. Which sex cells meet is a matter of chance. A grid can organize every possible pairing.
scenes.visual: Two mirrored sex-cell streams approach from the top and left. A green grid grows where they meet. One cell from each stream glides into every box while the other cells keep drifting.
scenes.narration: Fertilization brings one sex cell from each parent together. Which sex cells meet is a matter of chance. A grid can organize every possible pairing.

scenes.tts: Because each parent makes both sex-cell types equally often, every box has the same probability. The grid's area becomes a probability map.
scenes.visual: Divide the green grid into equal glowing areas. Yellow probability markers spread evenly across all boxes. On screen, show 1/2 along each parent edge and 1/4 inside every box.
scenes.narration: Because each parent makes both sex-cell types equally often, every box has the same probability. The grid's area becomes a probability map.

scenes.tts: Both parents can send either allele. Predict which pairing can make a white plant. Watch the allele cards before the flowers appear.
scenes.visual: Hold the empty green grid with P and p cards moving along its edges. Put a question mark inside every box. Do not show offspring genotypes or flower colors yet.
scenes.narration: Both parents can send either allele. Predict which pairing can make a white plant. Watch the allele cards before the flowers appear.

scenes.visual: Keep the prediction question on screen. Edge cards continue moving gently while the question marks breathe.

scenes.tts: White appears only when a small p arrives from both parents. The other pairings carry a dominant allele, so their flowers are purple.
scenes.visual: Drop the cards into the grid. Reveal PP, Pp, Pp and pp on screen. The pp box blooms white; the other boxes bloom purple. A soft ring circles the pp box.
scenes.narration: White appears only when a small p arrives from both parents. The other pairings carry a dominant allele, so their flowers are purple.

scenes.tts: Read genotype before phenotype. The genotype pattern has three groups. Complete dominance combines the first two groups into the same purple phenotype.
scenes.visual: Below the grid, build an on-screen genotype ratio from the boxes: 1 PP : 2 Pp : 1 pp. Transform it into a phenotype bar labelled 3 purple : 1 white. Keep all numbers visual only.
scenes.narration: Read genotype before phenotype. The genotype pattern has three groups. Complete dominance combines the first two groups into the same purple phenotype.

scenes.tts: The grid predicts the genotype pattern shown below it. Grouping by visible color gives the phenotype pattern. Both describe chances across repeated offspring.
scenes.visual: Pulse the genotype ratio, then the phenotype ratio. Send many schematic offspring icons past the grid into a running counter whose proportions wobble around the displayed predictions.
scenes.narration: The grid predicts the genotype pattern shown below it. Grouping by visible color gives the phenotype pattern. Both describe chances across repeated offspring.

scenes.tts: These four boxes are equally likely outcomes, not four promised offspring. A small batch may miss white entirely. Another batch may contain several.
scenes.visual: The grid becomes a probability wheel marked 25% per box. Run two schematic seed batches beside it. One batch grows all purple; another grows mixed colors. Label both outcomes possible, schematic.
scenes.narration: These four boxes are equally likely outcomes, not four promised offspring. A small batch may miss white entirely. Another batch may contain several.

scenes.tts: Alleles separate, and sex cells meet by chance. The square organizes those chances. It does not promise which offspring will arrive.
scenes.visual: Compress the whole carried world into one continuous path: paired allele cards separate, sex cells meet, and the grid fills. A yellow probability marker loops back to the next empty offspring spot.
scenes.narration: Alleles separate, and sex cells meet by chance. The square organizes those chances. It does not promise which offspring will arrive.

scenes.visual: Show one centered line only: 'Allele separation creates inheritance chances; Punnett squares organize, not guarantee, outcomes.'
